faq.q: How do I find middle C on the piano?
faq.a: Middle C is usually located near the center of the piano. You can find it by looking for the group of two black keys just to its left.
asks: Can you point out middle C?

faq.q: What is the difference between white and black keys?
faq.a: The white keys represent the main notes of the musical scale. The black keys represent notes called sharps or flats.
asks: Do the black keys mean something different?
What do the keys stand for?

faq.q: What does an octave mean when I play music?
faq.a: An octave is the interval between two notes that sound the same but are at different pitches. It is a complete cycle of notes.
asks: What is the range of an octave?
How far is an octave on the keyboard?
Does an octave mean the same note twice?

faq.q: Are there always groups of two or three black keys?
faq.a: Yes, the pattern of black keys is very consistent across the entire keyboard. They always appear in sets of two or sets of three.
asks: What is the black key pattern?
Do the black keys repeat a pattern?
Is the black key grouping random?

faq.q: If I play C up an octave, what do I get?
faq.a: You will play the note C again, but it will sound higher than the first one. This shows the full range of one octave.
asks: If I go up an octave, what note is it?
How do I know I reached an octave?

facts: White keys represent the main notes in the musical scale.
Black keys are arranged in repeating groups of two or three.
An octave covers the same note at two different pitches.
Middle C is a key reference point on most pianos.

quiz.say: Which keys are the main notes?
quiz.why: White keys represent the main notes in the musical scale.

wrong.0: Black keys represent notes called sharps and flats.
wrong.1: Octaves are a distance, not a key type.
wrong.2: Middle C is a specific note, not the whole group.

quiz.say: If you play a note and then play the same note higher up, what have you played?
quiz.why: An octave is the distance between the same note at two different pitches.

wrong.0: A scale is a sequence of notes, not just one interval.
wrong.1: A chord is playing several notes at the same time.
wrong.2: A pattern is too general a word for this musical term.

quiz.say: If you find the group of two black keys, the white key immediately to the right is likely:
quiz.why: The white keys are named notes, and the pattern helps you identify them.

wrong.0: A rest means silence, not a key.
wrong.1: Middle C is a specific location, not the general answer.
wrong.3: The keyboard continues far beyond the visible section.
